Harju Elekter Group AS Files for Insolvency Amid Mounting Pressures

Harju Elekter Group AS, a leading player in Estonia’s electrical equipment sector, has entered insolvency proceedings, casting uncertainty over the future of its operations and workforce. The company confirmed on Monday that it had commenced bankruptcy proceedings in Tallinn, citing “unsustainable market conditions and liquidity challenges.”

Production at Harju Elekter’s main plant in Keila has already slowed, with management stating that some assembly lines have been temporarily halted to preserve cash flow. “We are doing everything in our power to maintain critical functions and support our employees during this difficult period,” said Chief Executive Markus Laanemets in a statement. “Our immediate priority is to stabilize operations and seek solutions in cooperation with the administrators.”

The company employs approximately 450 people in Estonia, with additional staff in Latvia and Finland. According to the Estonian Electrical Industry Association, Harju Elekter’s insolvency could have “significant ripple effects” throughout the regional supply chain. “This is a major shock for the sector and will impact subcontractors and local suppliers,” said association chairperson Anneli Saar.

Analysts estimate that Harju Elekter Group AS accounts for around 12% of domestic switchgear and industrial cabling output. Orders have been delayed, and several clients are reportedly seeking alternative suppliers amid the uncertainty.

Representatives from the Elektritööliste Liit trade union urged the government to provide support for affected workers. “We are monitoring the situation closely and will advocate for every employee’s rights,” said union official Jaanus Mets.

The administrators are currently reviewing the company’s assets and liabilities, with further updates expected in the coming weeks.
